memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "She kept his cloak beside her until his master came home. Then she told him this story: 'That Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me. But as soon as I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.'" - Gen 39:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Potiphar's wife holds on to Joseph's cloak, waiting for her husband to return, and then repeats her false story to him. But notice a subtle, cutting detail: she calls Joseph "that Hebrew slave you brought us." In one phrase she shifts part of the blame onto Potiphar himself — as if to say, this is your fault for bringing this foreigner into our home. She is a skilled manipulator, weaving guilt and accusation together.

Here we see how deliberate and calculated a lie can be. This was no impulsive outburst; she kept the cloak as evidence, waited for the right moment, and shaped her words to manipulate her husband's emotions. Falsehood can be patient, planned, and persuasive. The truth had one silent witness — an empty cloak — while the lie had a confident, tearful voice.

It is sobering to realize how convincingly a lie can be told, and how a good person can be condemned by a false but well-crafted story. Joseph, who had done everything right, had no way to prove his innocence against such a tale.

This calls us to two things. First, let us be people who love and speak the truth, never using words to manipulate or destroy others (Eph 4:25). And second, when we are the ones wronged by lies, let us remember that God knows the truth even when no one else does. Human courts can be deceived, but the God who sees all cannot.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I always speak the truth, never twisting words to manipulate?
2. When I cannot prove my innocence, do I trust that God knows the truth?
3. How does it comfort me that God cannot be deceived?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me a person of truth who never uses words to harm others. And when I am wronged by lies I cannot disprove, comfort me with the truth that You see all and cannot be deceived. Amen.
